title: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding for Successive Refinement in Progressive Communication
authors: Qi Liao; Dario Bega
abstract: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth. We address this problem by proposing GO-OAE (Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding), which learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence, optimized directly for task utility rather than source reconstruction. Each component of the sequence is represented for transmission by its code index, and the learned ordering enables inference from any received prefix of the index sequence, with performance improving as more indices arrive. We prove that optimizing the goal-oriented distortion objective is equivalent to solving a weighted conditional information bottleneck formulation, and introduce an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator, to reduce GO-OAE training computational cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) with m << K, and reduces the estimator variance by a factor of 1/m. Experiments show that, on MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression vs. raw RGB), and already attains over 94% of the upper bound with only 70% of the transmitted indices. It consistently outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling across all transmission budgets, demonstrating effective communication at extreme compression rates.

title: Behavior-Mining, Generative Conversations, and Collaborative Advisory: the Future of Travel and Tourism Recommender Systems
authors: Alejandro Bellogín; Linus W. Dietz; Francesco Ricci; Pablo Sánchez
abstract: Since the early adoption of e-commerce, travel and tourism has been a lab for the design of recommender systems: tools that help travelers choose destinations, flights, accommodations, and combine them into itineraries. Data-driven recommendation techniques, ranging from case-based reasoning to reinforcement learning, have been adapted to travelers' needs. The research community has produced multifaceted prototypes of travel and tourism recommender systems (TTRSs), which are context-dependent, multistakeholder-oriented, and more recently, addressing sustainability issues, such as overtourism. Despite this enduring work, TTRSs are not widespread yet. We argue that three limitations can explain this: outdated and sparse data sets used to train and validate TTRSs, algorithms that prioritize prediction accuracy over domain-specific dimensions such as novelty and contextual relevance, and a failure to address the specific needs of travelers. Targeted incremental research could address these limitations, but a disruptive factor has meanwhile entered the ecosystem of tourism information and commercialization platforms: generative artificial intelligence. According to market research, GenAI applications are becoming the primary entry point for travelers planning their trips. This forces research to rethink how TTRSs should be designed and which core techniques should be integrated. We claim that future TTRSs, in addition to offering personalized information filtering, should become more flexible advisors that support decision making, integrating multiple data types and AI techniques, from data mining to natural language processing. Moreover, they must transparently balance the conflicting goals of travelers, service suppliers, platform owners, and local communities. We then outline research targets for building more effective TTRSs, fruitfully combining old and new recommendation techniques.

title: Mission Efficiency Optimization in Low-Altitude Economy: Adaptive Power Allocation for Coordinating Heterogeneous Aircraft Swarms
authors: Jiarui Zhang; Wei Feng; Chao Dong; Ning Ge; Qihui Wu
abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, low-altitude operations are booming, where complex missions require collaborative efforts among multiple heterogeneous low-altitude aircrafts (LAAs). Specifically, different LAAs assume distinct roles: some for sensing, some for communication, some for computing, and others for mission execution, together forming a sensing-communication-computing-control (SC3) closed loop, akin to a reflex arc. To enable efficient coordination in such multi-LAA swarms, we introduce the concept of operational-capability entropy (OCE) to quantify the effective work capability of operational LAAs. Accordingly, by jointly considering heterogeneous OCE and channel conditions among LAAs, we formulate the power allocation problem with the goal of minimizing the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost, which serves as a metric for mission efficiency. The resulting complex optimization problem is decomposed into two convex subproblems that are solved iteratively, with closed-form solutions derived for each. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed mission-oriented adaptive power allocation scheme significantly outperforms traditional ones.

title: Resource-Efficient Semantic Communication for Heterogeneous Agentic Teams
authors: Farhad Rezazadeh; Hatim Chergui; Lingjia Liu; Merouane Debbah
abstract: Teams of autonomous agents, including large language model (LLM) agents, must coordinate over scarce and unreliable wireless links. We propose goal-oriented semantic communication (GOSC), a closed-loop co-design that jointly decides what each agent sends, when it sends it, and how reliably it is transmitted, based on each message's value to the team task. An edge broadcast of the team's common knowledge closes the loop by updating these values. We prove that a message is sent only if its value exceeds the cost of delivering it and that more valuable messages receive more robust transmission rates, and we show that the scheduler solves each scheduling step exactly whenever the radio budget is not saturated, which held in 95% of scheduling decisions. In search-and-rescue missions validated on unseen scenarios, GOSC meets the same mission targets as carefully tuned periodic semantic schemes with 1.2--8.5 times fewer uplink channel uses. In most settings, this advantage persists with realistic packet overheads, reaching 16.6 times fewer uplink channel uses and 13.8 times lower cost when downlink costs are included; in the rescue task, it also persists when all agents share one uplink. Rough value estimates suffice, whereas values that ignore message content can fail. With three different LLMs, GOSC uses 3.2--3.5 times fewer channel uses, while completion-time gains depend on the model.

title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Korean Language Learning: Applications, Challenges, and Instructional Strategies
authors: Yundong Wu
abstract: This conceptual narrative review examines the role of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in Korean language learning. The paper synthesizes recent scholarship on AI-assisted language learning, Korean language education, technology acceptance, and educational ethics to develop an analytical framework for responsible classroom use. The review focuses on four dimensions: Korean language skills, Korean-specific linguistic and cultural features, instructional design, and governance risks. The analysis suggests that generative AI can support listening, speaking, reading, and writing when tasks are explicitly designed around Korean phonology, morphology, pragmatics, and learner purposes such as TOPIK preparation, study abroad, employment, and popular-culture engagement. It also identifies challenges in cultural-pragmatic accuracy, hallucinated expressions, assessment validity, data privacy, unequal access, teacher readiness, and learner dependency. The paper concludes that generative AI should function as a mediated learning resource rather than a substitute for teachers, learner judgment, or culturally grounded interaction.

title: Algorithmic Justice and Responsible AI Journalism: A Comparative Communication Policy Perspective in East Asia
authors: Renxiudi Huang; Linjia Bai
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence and automated content curation rapidly reshape the global media landscape, the intersection of algorithmic justice and media governance has become a critical frontier for sustainable development. This study provides a comparative communication policy analysis of China and South Korea, focusing explicitly on how their distinct regulatory toolkits address the tension between algorithmic fairness and platform accountability in AI journalism. While China utilizes a top-down, state-centric regulatory framework emphasizing ideological security, algorithmic registration, and strict synthetic media labeling, South Korea employs a multi-stakeholder co-regulation model driven by personal data protection, anti-monopoly platform intervention, and civil society oversight. Through a detailed textual analysis of key policy documents—including China's Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendations and South Korea's Guidelines for AI Service Ethics to Protect Users—alongside empirical evidence from prominent algorithmic news curation platforms (Toutiao and Naver), this paper evaluates the implementation efficacy and structural trade-offs of each nation's approach. We demonstrate that while both models mitigate the risks of digital infodemics and algorithmic bias, they face contrasting trade-offs between regulatory efficiency and editorial independence. Finally, this study introduces the "Policy-Media-Society" (PMS) responsive governance framework, clarifying how systemic institutional adaptations can advance UN Sustainable Development Goal 16 (SDG 16) by ensuring public access to transparent, verified information.

title: Research on Attention Guidance and User Autonomy in AI-Powered Immersive Environments
authors: Mulin Qiao
abstract: As artificial intelligence gets deeply embedded into immersive environments, attention-guiding technology delivers ever more precise and efficient outcomes. Still, this improved efficiency carries an overlooked design risk: excessive AI guidance may steadily erode user agency and undermine exploratory behaviors as well as the process of meaning-making. This paper builds a critical conceptual framework to rethink attention-oriented design within AI-driven immersive settings. It defines excessive guidance and establishes theoretical links between this concept and three core facets of user agency: perceived control, voluntary choice and decision-making authority. Based on these findings, the paper calls for a paradigm shift from attention optimization to curiosity-led design. It also puts forward actionable behavioral measurement indicators covering exploration scope, average dwell time, path-following ratio, active choice frequency and recall test performance. The proposed framework supplies a new theoretical tool for human-computer interaction research in immersive scenarios and helps shift AI's role from a fixed route provider to an exploratory collaborator.

title: Intersectional Realities and Adaptive Leadership: A Phenomenological Study of Black Women Administrators in Higher Education
authors: Jocelyn Vernet
venue: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University)
abstract: Existing literature consistently documents the acute underrepresentation of Black women in administrative leadership. Furthermore, Black women administrators that are represented and visible in higher education often oversee programs and task forces that heighten their experiences to high-risk situations. Emerging narratives suggest Black women employ effective coping strategies and embrace opportunities to strengthen and cultivate support networks while in their leadership roles. However, there is a significant lack in understanding how these strategies are structured and sustained to overcome the underrepresentation of Black women administrators in higher education. Additionally, basing their experiences solely through a survival lens limits a deeper understanding of their adaptability and the specific ways Black women leaders challenge the organizational norms and change structures within institutions. The purpose of this hermeneutic phenomenological study was to examine and interpret how Black women administrative leaders make meaning of their experiences and engage in adaptive leadership practices within their institutions. The researcher explored how participants described and made meaning of their leadership experiences while engaging with Adaptive Leadership. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with Black women administrative leaders from higher education institutions within the United States. In addition, participant transcript review occurred to ensure accuracy. Data were analyzed using hermeneutic phenomenological methods to identify meanings and interpret experiences across participants. Findings revealed a unique complexity for participants leading through institutional challenges, focusing others through change, and intergenerational responsibility. Despite experiences of racial and gendered discrimination, all 13 participants described varied forms of support as significant influencers of their professional growth and retention. Additionally, findings illuminated the shared communal obligation of invisible labor and expanding access for others. Furthermore, confidence in racial and gender identity and the power of voice and presence were crucial findings in which participants described as significantly important to embody as administrative leaders. Findings contribute to the growing body of literature related to Black woman administrative leaders in higher education and offer recommendations for educational leaders, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to improve institutional leadership and policy for Black women.

title: Building Intelligent Ethical Governance in the AI Era through AI-Based Prophetic Leadership for Institutional Transformation
authors: Masyhudi; Izzatul Munawwaroh; Eka Diana; Fachrurrozi; Angga Ade Saputra; Saiful Bahri
venue: JETech: Journal of Education and Technology
abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has accelerated institutional transformation through data analysis capabilities, process automation, and technology-based decision-making support. However, the increasing use of AI also presents ethical challenges related to transparency, accountability, algorithmic bias, and human responsibility in controlling technology. This study aims to explore how AI-Enabled Prophetic Leadership contributes to building Smart Ethical Governance to support sustainable institutional transformation. This study uses an exploratory qualitative approach involving 24 participants from three institutions that have implemented AI-based digital transformation. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observation, and document analysis, then analyzed using thematic analysis techniques. The results of the study show three main findings, namely: (1) the reconstruction of prophetic leadership values (shiddiq, amanah, tabligh, and fathanah) into dimensions of digital integrity, moral accountability, communicative transparency, and ethical intelligence; (2) the integration of prophetic leadership and AI through human-centered decision-making, algorithmic oversight, system transparency, and strengthening organizational competencies; and (3) institutional transformation through structural, cultural, and operational changes. This research produces a conceptual model of the AI-Based Prophetic Ethical Governance Model (APEGM) that positions prophetic leadership as the foundation of values, AI as a decision-support instrument, and human oversight as a technology control mechanism. This research provides theoretical contributions to the development of ethical leadership and AI governance studies and provides practical implications for institutions in building innovative, responsible, and human-value-oriented digital transformations.

title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
authors: Muh. Noval Fuaddillah; Ummul Fadilah; Maripaz C. Abas
venue: JETech: Journal of Education and Technology
abstract: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. Meanwhile, teachers assume a facilitative role by guiding inquiry, supporting experimentation, and connecting technical knowledge with authentic problems. This study highlights the pedagogical value of integrating Design Thinking into technology education as a framework for connecting computational competencies with human-centered innovation. Its implications emphasize the importance of designing learning activities that balance technical proficiency, creative exploration, and meaningful student participation.

title: Krum-Inspired Central Teacher Selection and Residual Channel Bottlenecks for Efficient DeepSC
authors: Rami Eid; Mostafa Jammoul; Omar Kaaki; Maria Slim; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deploying transformer-based semantic communication models on edge devices requires compression that preserves semantic fidelity under channel variability. We study a compressed deep semantic communication (DeepSC) student trained by multi-teacher knowledge distillation and combine two ideas: (i) a residual channel bottleneck that splits the transmitted representation into a base stream and a residual stream with unequal power allocation, and (ii) a Krum-inspired, medoid-style centrality criterion that selects a single central teacher from a five-model ensemble, applied at the logit and intermediate-feature levels and combined with a feature-dominant distillation loss. On the EuroParl benchmark, a two-layer student recovers about 98% of the four-layer teacher's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU)-1 under additive white Gaussian noise, with 93% of its BLEU-4 and 96% of its sentence-BERT (SBERT) score, and about 89%, 77%, and 87% of the teacher's BLEU-1, BLEU-4, and SBERT, respectively, under Rayleigh fading, while reducing non-embedding parameters by 1.33x and single-teacher inference latency by 1.79x (9.0x relative to a five-teacher ensemble used here as an upper-bound reference, not a deployment baseline). Controlled ablations over three seeds indicate complementary contributions of about +8.4% BLEU-1 (+9.6% SBERT) from the residual bottleneck and +3.0% (+2.9% SBERT) from centrality-based selection over mean aggregation. A decoder-mode ablation shows that the base stream alone recovers about two-thirds of the full BLEU-1 while the residual stream alone collapses, supporting the role of the residual as a refinement on top of the base.

title: Where to Defend? Layer-Wise Adversarial Training for Robust Transformer-Based Semantic Communications
authors: Maria Slim; Razane Tajeddine; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC), a Transformer-based encoder-decoder, achieves semantic fidelity over noisy channels but remains vulnerable to adversarial perturbations injected at multiple stages of the pipeline. We present a layer-wise robustness framework that compares fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projected gradient descent (PGD), and l2-normalized fast gradient method (FGM) defenses at the embedding output, and then uses PGD to analyze three attack and defense points: the embedding output, encoder output, and channel-encoder bottleneck. We evaluate reconstruction on Europarl and UK Hansard and sentiment classification on SST2 and YELP under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading. A first-order damage budget, {epsilon} times the l1 norm of the clean-input loss gradient at each injection point, predicts the attack-severity ordering, and the transfer matrix reveals asymmetric defense transfer: the embedding defense transfers strongly to encoder attacks, whereas encoder defenses degrade robustness against upstream attacks. For reconstruction, encoder-point training yields the largest matched gain but fails severely under embedding attacks; joint embedding-plus-encoder training retains comparable gains under encoder attacks while mitigating this mismatch failure, and Rayleigh fading attenuates robustness gains and degradation. For classification, three of four defenses collapse to constant predictors; only the channel-encoder defense remains non-degenerate, suggesting a protective role for the 128D-to-16D bottleneck. At a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 9 dB and perturbation budget {epsilon} = 0.3, the matched encoder defense recovers bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) from ~ 0.10 to ~ 0.64 on Europarl/AWGN, whereas the mismatched encoder defense yields a -0.444 BLEU change relative to the undefended baseline under an embedding attack.

title: Semantic-Aware Sub-Band Allocation for Terahertz Communications
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: This paper studies semantic-aware sub-band al- location for terahertz (THz) communication systems, where frequency-selective molecular absorption creates highly non- uniform sub-band qualities. Unlike conventional formulations, semantic fidelity depends nonlinearly on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and is also sentence-specific, leading to a non-separable assignment problem that is generally not solvable using simple ordering-based policies. To address this, we use a sentence-BERT (SBERT)-based surrogate model that predicts semantic fidelity from the sentence embedding and sub-band SNR. We propose an importance-aware scheduler that assigns sentences to sub- bands based on their semantic contribution using an oracle utility function that captures importance-weighted semantic similarity across sentence-sub-band pairs. A neural scheduler is then trained through imitation learning to approximate the oracle policy at more than 200x lower runtime than full DeepSC- based oracle evaluation. Integrated with a deep-learning-enabled semantic communication (DeepSC) system, the proposed method consistently outperforms all benchmark schemes and approaches oracle-level performance under realistic THz channel conditions.

title: Flexible Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding: A Vibrotactile Example
authors: Shuijie Li; Kemi Chen; Runjie Wang; Tiesong Zhao; Xiaoming Tao
abstract: The increasing demand for real-time tactile communication in multimedia systems has exposed the limitations of existing Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) techniques. While current JSCC models facilitate end-to-end optimization, they typically operate at fixed coding rates and require separate model instances for different rate settings. This results in significant storage overhead and limited adaptability to dynamic bandwidth conditions. To address these challenges, we propose the Flexible Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding (FD-JSCC) framework for vibrotactile signals, which supports flexible-rate transmission without the need for model switching. The FD-JSCC integrates a flexible-rate encoder-decoder enhanced with Hierarchical Gain Adaptation Module (HGAM) and Rate-Switchable Residual Module (RSRM), enabling bitrate-aware compression by selectively preserving salient vibrotactile features. Additionally, we introduce a Channel Feature Processing Module (CFPM), which leverages real-time SNR information to enhance robustness against channel noise and signal degradation. Trained on the IEEE 1918.1.1 vibrotactile dataset, FD-JSCC achieves reconstruction performance comparable to fixed-rate baselines (e.g., DeepSC-S), while reducing storage requirements by 61.1\% when supporting four rates. These results underscore its potential for scalable, low-latency tactile communication in next-generation networks.

title: Compressibility is not Feedback: A Random-access Gap in Causal Semantic Repair
authors: Milad Bafarassat
abstract: Semantic feedback can repair a noisy first decode without retransmitting the whole message, but current end-to-end evaluations hide where a feedback design fails. An oracle that sees both the source-side state and receiver observation may describe a useful correction with few bits, while the receiver, which sees only its own observation, may not know which correction to request. We formulate these as distinct direct and receiver-constrained coding problems, connect repair distortion to retained local utility and prove a random-access separation: one direct bit is exact although receiver utility vanishes with the number of source-conditioned alternatives. A synthetic ladder verifies the exact law. In paired populations of eight Reuters text-JSCC codecs, the trained recurrent population retains over three times more direct 16-bit repair value than the trained DeepSC population despite comparable full-repair opportunity. Nevertheless, an entropy-valid receiver audit across all eight recurrent checkpoints does not resolve against repetition, source-only or shuffled-index controls. The results show that compressible repair is an upper bound, not evidence of deployable feedback, and motivate reporting both rate curves under matched resources.
arxiv_comment: The author withdraws this paper because the operational upper-bound interpretation of the direct/oracle repair results in Sections 3.3 and 4.3 is not established. The implemented repair and compression procedures provide achievable benchmarks rather than certified upper bounds on receiver-constrained performance, undermining the interpretation of the experimental comparison

title: SignDeepSC: A Semantic Signature-based Approach for Robust Semantic Communication
authors: Khalil Alhaj; Razane Tajeddine; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Semantic communication systems such as deep semantic communication (DeepSC) offer high efficiency but are vulnerable to adversarial attacks on their underlying neural networks. We address a physical-layer man-in-the-middle (MitM) threat in which an adversary injects perturbations into the transmitted signal to distort its meaning. We propose SignDeepSC, an architectural defense that achieves adversarial robustness without requiring explicit adversarial example generation during training. The approach is built on a perceiver-inspired semantic signature, a compact vector summary of the source features transmitted over a separate low-rate auxiliary channel. This signature is used by a self-repairing decoder that leverages cross-attention to correct distortions and can additionally drive a scrambler that shuffles the feature layout. We evaluate SignDeepSC over Rayleigh fading and additive white Gaussian noise channels under both single-step fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and iterative projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. Under PGD ($ε= 0.7$), at 12~dB signal-to-noise ratio with Rayleigh fading, SignDeepSC achieves a bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU-4) score of 0.237 and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) sentence similarity of 0.646, outperforming all baselines without degrading clean-channel performance, when the signature channel is well protected.

title: Structured Spectral Compression based Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications for Internet of Things assisted Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Li Ping Qian; Zhehan Chen; Qianru Wang; Qian Wang; Yuan Wu; Xuemin Sherman Shen
abstract: This paper focuses on the Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications based on the Structured Spectral Compression (LB-S2C2). Specifically, the Mel spectral matrix of the speech signal is first encoded at the transmitter side through compressive sensing based on waveform segmentation and data quantization. Then, the Automatic Repeat Request (ARQ) is combined with forward error correction to achieve reliable transmission of speech signals over wireless channels. Thirdly, the received signals are recovered as the speech at the receiver side. Finally, we conduct a series of simulation experiments for the performance evaluation of LB-S2C2. Our simulations reveal that the dictionary matrix used for the speech reconstruction is different from the one used for the high-order matrix sparsification by even only approximately 0.1%, and then the accurate speech recovery fails. It implies that the speech data can be securely transmitted when the dictionary matrix is preserved. More importantly, the LB-S2C2 exhibits a very high privacy protection capability with the average voiceprint similarity to be only 0.3, which is much lower than the 0.8 of the semantic speech communication scheme DeepSC-S, and even lower than the 0.33 of the latest speech communication scheme OFI-OFCNB. In addition, our simulations reveal that the proposed structured speech coding boasts a time complexity of merely O(n), and the proposed speech recovery scheme requires the 12-bit memory storage only, which outperforms the traditional encryption algorithms proposed for speech communications. In comparison with the conventional compression techniques, our spectral compression method renders the coding rate of only 3.9kbps, which is lower than the current lowest speech coding rate of 6.3kbps achieved by G.723.

title: Semantic Communications in the THz Band
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: Semantic and terahertz (THz)-band communications are algorithmic and spectral enablers of future wireless networks. This work investigates deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC) over THz channels. We show that DeepSC models trained solely under additive white Gaussian noise generalize well to the tested THz block- and fast-fading channels when receiver-side compensation is applied. To enable fully data-driven reception, we propose a lightweight neural detector that does not require channel state information (CSI). At 0.3 THz, DeepSC outperforms a throughput-matched traditional coded communication system baseline over 0-12 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), achieving more than 50 percentage-point higher Bilingual Evaluation Understudy unigram (BLEU-1) score. The proposed pilot-free detector outperforms minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization with both perfect and imperfect CSI and remains robust to frequency offsets up to 50 MHz, highlighting the resilience of semantic communication to THz channel impairments.

title: Image Semantic Communication with Quadtree Partition-based Coding
authors: Yinhuan Huang; Zhijin Qin
abstract: Deep learning based semantic communication (DeepSC) system has emerged as a promising paradigm for efficient wireless transmission. However, existing image DeepSC methods, frequently encounter challenges in balancing rate-distortion performance and computational complexity, and often exhibit inferior performance compared to traditional schemes, especially on high-resolution datasets. To address these limitations, we propose a novel image DeepSC system, using quadtree partition-based joint semantic-channel coding, named Quad-DeepSC, which maintains low complexity while achieving state-of-the-art transmission performance. Based on maturing learned image compression technologies, we establish a unified DeepSC system design and training pipeline. The proposed Quad-DeepSC integrates quadtree partition-based entropy estimation and feature coding modules with lightweight feature extraction and reconstruction networks to form an end-to-end architecture. During training, all components except the feature coding modules are jointly optimized as a compact learned image codec, Quad-LIC, for source compression tasks. The pretrained Quad-LIC is then embedded into Quad-DeepSC and fine-tuned end-to-end over wireless channels. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Quad-DeepSC is the first DeepSC system to surpass conventional communication systems, which employ VTM for source coding and adopt the optimal MCS index under 3GPP standards for channel coding and digital modulation, in performance across datasets of varying resolutions. Notably, both Quad-DeepSC and Quad-LIC exhibit minimal latency, rendering them well-suited for deployment in real-time wireless communication systems.

title: VQ-VAE Based Digital Semantic Communication with Importance-Aware OFDM Transmission
authors: Ming Lyu; Hao Chen; Dan Wang; Chen Qiu; Guangyin Feng; Nan Ma; Xiaodong Xu
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) significantly reduces redundant data and improves transmission efficiency by extracting the latent features of information. However, most of the conventional deep learning-based SemCom systems focus on analog transmission and lack in compatibility with practical digital communications. This paper proposes a vector quantized-variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) based digital SemCom system that directly transmits the semantic features and incorporates the importance-aware orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) transmission to enhance the SemCom performance, where the VQ-VAE generates a discrete codebook shared between the transmitter and receiver. At transmitter, the latent semantic features are firstly extracted by VQ-VAE, and then the shared codebook is adopted to match these features, which are subsequently transformed into a discrete version to adapt the digital transmission. To protect the semantic information, an importance-aware OFDM transmission strategy is proposed to allocate the key features near the OFDM reference signals, where the feature importance is derived from the gradient-based method. At the receiver, the features are rematched with the shared codebook to further correct errors. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional DeepSC and achieves better reconstruction performance under low SNR region.

title: QISFP: a quantum-inspired semantic fidelity protocol for energy-efficient and noise-resilient visual IoT transmission
authors: David Elias Emmanuel; Anil Fernando
abstract: Abstract Visual Internet of Things deployments operate under coupled bandwidth, energy and channel-reliability constraints, yet conventional video coding optimises pixel-level reconstruction rather than the preservation of task-relevant meaning. This paper presents QISFP, a quantum-inspired semantic fidelity protocol that treats semantic degradation as a stochastic state transformation rather than as additive signal distortion. It couples delta encoding of temporally associated object-level semantic states with a stochastic channel built from classical analogues of the depolarizing and amplitude-damping maps, and reconstructs meaning by energy- and confidence-weighted fusion over a temporal window. The framework is classical throughout: the quantum formalism supplies trace-preserving maps whose diagonal restriction is a stochastic matrix, which keeps per-object cost linear rather than quadratic in the semantic dimension. The induced class channel is shown to be $$M$$ M -ary symmetric, yielding two independent decay constants that characterise a semantic link and fix a multi-hop relaying budget, while a source-channel separation argument gives the attainability limit $$F \le 1 - p_d(1-1/M)$$ F ≤ 1 - p d ( 1 - 1 / M ) , met with equality by uncoded single-observation transmission; every attainable gain therefore lies in the temporal dimension. Simulation on CDNet 2014 and UCF-101 indicates 27.5% lower energy per frame and 30.3% lower transmitted volume than full-frame x264, with semantic fidelity of 0.922 against 0.855 for a frame-wise semantic baseline, at a cost of 1.28 dB in PSNR. An end-to-end measurement on detector output tests the theory directly: the frame-wise baseline tracks the single-use limit to within 0.022 IoU, the framework exceeds that limit wherever the channel is non-trivial, and at matched fidelity it requires between 42% and 64% fewer bits than the baseline. The protocol requires a few kilobytes of state and fewer than $$10^4$$ 10 4 operations per frame, so embedded feasibility is governed by the choice of semantic extractor rather than by QISFP itself.

title: Adaptive Channel Coding with Semantic-Aware Error Protection for 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Ambar Bajpai
abstract: Abstract Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) — comprising low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, high-altitude platform stations (HAPS), and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) — are increasingly regarded as a foundational layer of sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, extending connectivity to rural, maritime, and disaster-affected regions that remain beyond the economic reach of terrestrial infrastructure. NTN links, however, present a uniquely hostile channel environment: long and time-varying propagation delay, large Doppler shifts induced by high relative platform velocity, deep fades from atmospheric and rain attenuation, and severe constraints on onboard power and computation. Conventional fixed-rate or classically-adaptive channel coding schemes, which react only to instantaneous signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), are poorly matched to this environment: they either over-provision redundancy, wasting scarce bandwidth and energy, or under-provision it and trigger the so-called cliff effect, in which a small SNR drop causes catastrophic decoding failure. In this paper we propose semantic-aware adaptive channel coding (SA-ACC), a framework that couples semantic importance estimation with rate- and redundancy-adaptive coding so that error-protection resources are allocated according to the task-relevant meaning of transmitted content rather than uniformly across all bits. We formalize the system model for a representative NTN scenario — a LEO downlink relayed through a HAPS node — define a semantic importance metric derived from task-gradient sensitivity, and design a two-stage adaptation control loop that jointly selects code rate, modulation order, and per-feature protection level under explicit delay and energy budgets. We further specify a complete evaluation methodology, comparing SA-ACC against fixed-rate LDPC/polar coding, conventional adaptive coding and modulation (ACM), and non-semantic deep joint source-channel coding (JSCC) across bit error rate, block error rate, semantic fidelity, throughput, latency, and energy metrics, and use this methodology to reason about SA-ACC’s expected behavior ahead of full numerical validation. Our architectural analysis indicates that SA-ACC should be able to sustain task-relevant reconstruction quality at lower effective SNR than baselines optimized purely at the bit level, at the cost of additional encoder and decoder complexity that we discuss explicitly. We close by outlining the simulation and ablation study required to convert this design-and-methodology contribution into a fully validated result.

title: Resource optimization for RIS-UAV integrated air-ground cooperative semantic communication driven by deep reinforcement learning
authors: Yufei Dai; Yuanyuan Yao; Sai Huang; Xinwei Yue
abstract: To meet the 6G semantic transmission requirements, this paper proposes an air-ground dual-mode semantic transmission architecture for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-aided Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. By dynamically assigning RIS-reflected links to users with long packets and direct UAV line-of-sight (LOS) links to users with short packets, we jointly optimize semantic symbols, RIS phase shifts, UAV three-dimensional (3D) trajectory, and transmit power to maximize the system-level semantic Quality of Experience (QoE). To efficiently solve the formulated non-convex mixed-integer optimization problem, we present an Action Space Decoupled Hybrid Deep Reinforcement Learning (ASD-HDRL) framework, which employs the Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) for discrete semantic resource decision-making and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) for continuous control optimization. Simulation results verify that the proposed ASD-HDRL achieves superior system-level semantic QoE performance.

title: Semantic SCL Decoding for Polar Codes
authors: Andy Huang; Chentao Yue; Branka S. Vucetic; Yonghui Li
abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for improving communication reliability by exploiting the inherent structure and semantic dependencies of transmitted information. This paper proposes a semantic successive cancellation list (SCL) decoder for polar codes carrying natural-language text. A fine-tuned byte-level language model provides next-byte priors, which are converted into conditional bit costs and incorporated directly into the SCL path metric before each pruning step. This allows the decoder to jointly exploit channel reliability and source structure while retaining the conventional polar coding framework. The language model can also be invoked only for bytes whose channel decisions are unreliable, trading decoding performance for latency. Simulations for length-512 polar codes show substantial block error rate (BLER) improvements over conventional CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) decoding. At rate R=0.75 and list size L=16, the proposed decoder achieves more than 1 dB of gain in BLER compared to CA-SCL with the same L. Moreover, with L=8, it outperforms conventional CA-SCL with L=256 in terms of BLER, while requiring about one quarter of the decoding time of the latter in the evaluated software implementation.

title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
authors: Xiaotian Xu; Zhifeng Tang; Guangchen Wang; Nan Yang; Xiangyun Zhou; Salman Durrani; Yansha Deng
abstract: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.

title: Guess and Send: World-Model-Guided Semantic Packet Transmission for Robust Video Perception
authors: Yan Gong; Zheng Chu; Wei Koong Chai; Hari Mohan Pandey; Jiankang Zhang; Jingrui Hou; Miao Zhang; Y. Li; Pei Xiao
abstract: Reliable video perception over bandwidth-constrained wireless links requires transmitting information that the receiver cannot already recover from its evolving scene representation. This paper introduces Guess and Send, a world-model-guided semantic packet transmission framework that prioritizes information according to its contribution to the receiver's perception. A shared feature-space world model predicts the receiver's scene state through affine motion compensation and learned residual displacement, while sender-side verification identifies reusable predictions. An acknowledgment-synchronized receiver twin estimates task-impact scores through two counterfactual evaluations, guiding packet selection and unequal error protection over LDPC-coded wireless channels. A compact 3-bit feature representation increases spatial coverage under stringent bandwidth constraints, while predictive fallback sustains perception during packet outages. Experiments on KITTI-MOTS (KITTI) and VisDrone2019-MOT (VisDrone) under Rayleigh fading and AWGN demonstrate substantial gains in low-SNR conditions. On KITTI at a 4.13% reference bandwidth budget, Guess and Send achieves 47.5% J&F at 0 dB Rayleigh SNR, outperforming H.264 by 11.3 percentage points. Controlled ablations show that world-model prediction contributes up to 8.7 points under Rayleigh fading. Object-detection experiments further demonstrate the transferability of receiver-relative predictive transmission across visual perception tasks. These results establish world-model-guided, receiver-state-aware transmission as an effective approach to robust video perception under severe communication constraints.

title: Semantic Communications: Principles, Architectures and Applications
authors: Sasa Maric
abstract: Conventional communication systems are designed to transmit data reliably, focusing on metrics such as bit error rate, throughput, and channel capacity. However, these traditional measures do not evaluate whether the received information is actually useful for a specific downstream task. To address this limitation, semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm that prioritizes the meaning, context, and task relevance of transmitted information rather than raw bit level reconstruction. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the theoretical foundations, system architectures, learning techniques, and evaluation practices in semantic communications. We classify existing state-of-the-art algorithms ranging from deep joint source-channel coding (Deep JSCC) and task-oriented feature transmission to generative diffusion models and contrast their operational trade offs against conventional baselines. Furthermore, we examine key application domains, including remote sensing, autonomous vehicles, and healthcare IoT, while addressing open challenges in security, privacy, robustness, and standardized evaluation.

title: AI-ENABLED SEMANTIC COMMUNICATION ARCHITECTURE FOR 6G NETWORKS: AN INTELLIGENT, CONTEXT-AWARE AND RESOURCE-EFFICIENT FRAMEWORK WITH HYBRID OPTIMIZATION
authors: Ganesan S.; Jagatheeshkumar G.
venue: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
abstract: Communication architectures that can enable intelligent services, vast connectivity, ultra-low latency, and extremely heterogeneous applications are necessary due to the sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks' rapid expansion. Large amounts of redundant data are communicated with significant bandwidth, energy, and computational overhead since conventional communication systems are primarily concerned with correct bit-level transmission. By conveying task-relevant meaning rather than full raw data, semantic communication overcomes this constraint. This research presents an AI-Enabled Semantic Communication Architecture for 6G Networks that combines context-aware decision-making, intelligent semantic extraction, and hybrid optimization. Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO) optimizes transmission parameters and semantic reconstruction quality, whereas Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) selects semantic features and allocates communication resources in the suggested framework. The optimization method is dynamically modified by a context-aware semantic controller based on network resources, channel conditions, and application needs. The framework is intended to maximize semantic similarity and communication efficiency while minimizing semantic distortion, latency, energy usage, and bandwidth utilization. Text-based semantic communication is used in an experimental assessment framework with different network loads and signal-to-noise ratios. For upcoming 6G applications, the suggested architecture offers a basis for resource-efficient, flexible, and intelligent semantic communication.

title: State-Aware Virtual Patient Simulation for Training Psychiatrists in Challenging Clinical Scenarios
authors: Harsh Mohta; C Chandrahas Reddy; Sunhith Reddy Bojja; Manik Inder Singh Sethi; Vinesh Gupta; Raghuram Bharadwaj Diddigi
abstract: Psychiatrists must be prepared to manage patients exhibiting challenging psychological states, including suicidal ideation, hallucinations, and other high-risk behaviors. However, opportunities to safely practice such interactions are limited. While recent conversational agents can simulate patients, existing approaches largely rely on large language models (LLMs) to determine patient responses, making it difficult to consistently maintain psychological state, adapt to the clinician's responses, and generate clinically plausible challenges that meaningfully test the clinician. We present a state-aware virtual patient simulation pipeline for training psychiatrists in challenging clinical scenarios. The proposed system maintains an evolving patient state throughout the interaction and orchestrates patient behavior rather than leaving response generation entirely to an LLM. At each interaction, a learning-based behavioral strategy selector determines the type and level of challenge appropriate to the current patient and clinician context. The selected strategy, patient state, clinician response, interaction history, and relevant clinical knowledge are then provided as grounded context to an LLM to generate a semantically relevant and psychologically consistent patient response. Following each session, the system analyzes the interaction and provides feedback to the clinician on their communication and management of the virtual patient.

title: SparseLift: Automatically Optimizing Opaque Sparse Paths in Industrial-Scale Recommendation Model Training
authors: Changqing Shi; Anan Liu; Genbao Chen; Junchao Yang
abstract: The sparse path, comprising sparse operations and collective communication, is a critical component of large-scale recommendation models. However, these operations are often represented as opaque nodes in the training computation graph, hindering whole-graph optimization. We present SparseLift, a low-overhead compiler for the sparse path of large-scale recommendation training. It exposes sparse computation and communication to whole-graph analysis to expand the optimization space and improve training efficiency. By analyzing model structure and runtime information, SparseLift reconstructs opaque nodes as analyzable subgraphs, recovering the resource semantics of sparse computation and communication within the graph. Building on the recovered semantics, we design incremental cost models and a constraint-aware planner to automatically select and organize subgraph optimizations into an execution plan that is reused during subsequent steady-state training. We evaluate SparseLift on an industrial video-platform recommendation task with 100B sparse parameters and the public DLRM benchmark. SparseLift improves steady-state throughput for ordinary industrial training steps by 16.5\% over the native baseline. On DLRM, it achieves $1.60\times$ and $1.26\times$ model-execution speedups over DLRM-Baseline and TorchRec, respectively.

title: RadPose: ISAC-based RF 3D Human Pose Estimation
authors: Geo Jie Zhou; Kunzhe Song; Ruxin Lin; Huacheng Zeng
abstract: Human pose estimation under adverse lighting and occlusion conditions remains challenging for camera- and LiDAR-based systems. Although mmWave radars provide robustness to illumination and occlusion, they rely on dedicated hardware and licensed spectrum, limiting scalability. In this paper, we present RadPose, a learning-based monostatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that enables mmWave communication devices to perform 3D human pose estimation. Unlike specialized radars, RadPose leverages monostatic full-duplex operation to extract channel impulse responses (CIRs) directly from standard OFDM communication signals, generating 3D radio point clouds without additional sensing hardware. To address the sparsity and noise of RF observations, RadPose employs a cross-frame transformer-based pose inference network with semantic-guided spatial attention and target-driven temporal attention for robust spatio-temporal aggregation. It further adopts a joint-aware inverse kinematics refinement module based on graph convolution to enforce skeletal topology, bone-length consistency, and anatomical plausibility. Extensive experiments demonstrate RadPose achieves competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art radar-based approaches while maintaining robust performance in unseen and occluded scenarios. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/Geo-Chou/RadPose.

title: ASNER: Software Architecture Recovery with Adaptive Semantic Neighborhoods and Evidence-Grounded Refinement
authors: Wenhao Wang; Zhi Jin; Jia Li; Dongming Jin; Heng Tian; Yingtao Fang; Wenguang Ye; Tiankuo Zhao
abstract: Automated software architecture recovery provides architectural context for software engineering and repository-level LLM agents. Existing methods combine structural and semantic signals, but functional relatedness does not necessarily imply shared architectural responsibility. Fixed thresholds or Top-K neighborhoods also ignore repository scale and local similarity distributions, introducing errors that propagate through clustering. Unconstrained LLM refinement may further alter correct assignments without sufficient evidence. We propose ASNER (Adaptive Semantic Neighborhoods and Evidence-Grounded Refinement for Software Architecture Recovery), based on responsibility-aware, project-adaptive relation modeling and evidence-grounded boundary verification. ASNER derives structured file responsibilities with an LLM, constructs semantic neighborhoods that adapt to repository scale and local similarity distributions, and augments a static dependency graph with selected semantic relations and weak directory cues. Community detection recovers the component backbone. A Responsibility-Ownership-Aware (ROA) Agent then examines uncertain boundary files using project-level responsibilities and traceable code evidence, changing assignments only when supported. Experiments on 12 open-source projects spanning C, C++, Java, and Python show that ASNER achieves the best macro-average on all five metrics on the common benchmark, improving ARI and c2c@66 over GAER-GAT by 19.5% and 32.9%, respectively. A downstream evaluation shows that ASNER-guided LocAgent improves file-, module-, and function-level code localization, demonstrating the value of its architectural context for repository-level software engineering tasks.

title: Collective Emergent Alignment: Measuring and Amplifying Interaction-Induced Reasoning Alignment in Multi-Agent LLMs
authors: Boxuan Wang; Zhuoyun Li; Sarvapali D. Ramchurn; Xiaowei Huang; Yi Dong
abstract: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems can exhibit emergent behaviors through interaction, yet whether a similar phenomenon exists for reasoning alignment remains largely unexplored. We study whether agent interaction produces additional reference-grounded reasoning alignment beyond matched individual self-refinement, and introduce REMAP (Reference-Entailment-Matrix for Agentic Process), a framework that quantifies this effect through Semantic Coverage and interaction-specific alignment gains. Across diverse model families and two multi-hop reasoning benchmarks, we observe broadly positive interaction gains, particularly on reasoning content that depends on integrating evidence distributed across agents. These gains are consistently associated with independently measured peer-information recovery, while further analysis reveals composition-dependent heterogeneity effects and asymmetric information transfer across agent capability levels. Motivated by these findings, we further introduce a fact-level multi-agent communication framework that replaces full reasoning-trace exchange with compact, gap-aware, and selectively routed information. Our experiments show that compact fact exchange improves reasoning alignment and task performance while reducing communication overhead, whereas more selective communication exposes a trade-off between acquiring distributed information, retaining local content, and communication efficiency. Overall, our results show that collective emergent alignment can be quantified, linked to information-transfer patterns, and used to guide more effective multi-agent communication.

title: CON-SENSO. Reflections on Applied Anthropology On the Right to Health and Informed Consent
authors: Stefania Spada
venue: Directory of Open access Books (OAPEN Foundation)
abstract: Does informed consent truly guarantee a subjective, free, and informed right to health for everyone, without discrimination? In other words, does informed consent—as it is actually practiced—serve as a guarantor of rights? This paper will attempt to answer these questions by presenting the findings of an anthropological study conducted in the gynecology and obstetrics department of a university hospital in the Emilia-Romagna region. Drawing on philosophical and legal reflections, the author examines the capacity of fundamental rights—and in particular the right to health—to become substantive in the contemporary intercultural context. Enforceability in everyday practice must, in fact, be understood by considering the various dimensions of power that characterize relationships, first and foremost the doctor-patient relationship. Throughthe ethnography of healthcare practices, the ways in which informed consent is implemented engage in a dialogue with reflections on the critical issues and dysfunctions inherent in the corporate logic that structures the encounter between biomedical knowledge and citizens.
keywords: semantic-aware communication; semantic transmission; semantic channel coding

title: OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding with One-Step Diffusion
authors: Shunpu Tang; Qianqian Yang
abstract: Neural joint source-channel coding (JSCC) enables efficient image transmission over noisy channels, yet distortion-optimized approaches often produce blurry reconstructions. While diffusion priors can enhance visual fidelity, their iterative sampling incurs substantial decoding latency. To address this limitation, we propose OSD-JSCC, an SNR-adaptive JSCC framework with a single diffusion step. Specifically, OSD-JSCC transmits pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) latents through an SNR-conditioned JSCC codec and incorporates two key designs. First, we introduce a stochastic diffusion-state interface that enables the JSCC decoder to predict a Gaussian diffusion state rather than a clean latent, while extracting image-specific semantic tokens. The sampled diffusion state preserves spatial structure and provides a good initialization for one-step refinement, whereas the semantic tokens, together with an SNR token, guide the reconstruction process. Second, we develop SNR-conditioned feature modulation and adaptive timestep selection to jointly adapt latent transmission and diffusion refinement to varying channel conditions. Furthermore, we adopt a three-stage training strategy with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to efficiently adapt the pretrained diffusion prior to the JSCC task. Extensive experiments on Kodak and CLIC2020 demonstrate that OSD-JSCC achieves superior perceptual quality and decoding efficiency. Compared with existing diffusion-based JSCC baselines, OSD-JSCC reduces LPIPS by approximately 43% on Kodak and 53% on CLIC2020, while achieving up to a 50.6$\times$ reduction in decoding latency.

title: MirrorComm: A Communication-Efficient Cooperative Perception Framework via Mirrored World Models
authors: Shenghan Luo; Yin Xu; Cixiao Zhang; Yang Wang; Yujie Cao; Zhuoran Xiao; Wenjun Zhang
abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) requires substantial communication bandwidth to exchange sensing information among connected agents. A variety of compression techniques have been proposed to reduce transmission costs while retaining task-relevant information. However, most existing methods follow a frame-wise compression paradigm, overlooking temporal predictability and repeatedly transmitting information that could be inferred from historical context. To address these limitations, we propose MirrorComm, the first world model-based communication-efficient CP framework. Specifically, mirrored world models at the transmitter and receiver predict the transmitter's current observation from a shared history of its reconstructed observations. The transmitter compares this prediction with its current observation and selectively transmits observation updates to correct prediction errors, reducing repeated transmission of predictable information. Experiments on the OPV2V dataset across two downstream tasks including object detection and semantic segmentation show that MirrorComm reduces communication bandwidth requirements by up to approximately 66-fold while maintaining comparable performance to a state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components.

title: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission
authors: Yifan Feng; Chentao Yue; Haiyao Yu; Gaoyang Pang; Xinyu Chen; Hao Chang; Branka Vucetic; Yonghui Li
abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) can correct the residual errors of a standard channel code with a foundation model that supplies a prior on the source content, but existing SECC schemes are designed for text. In this paper, we develop SECC for image transmission with spatial token interleaving and a two-pass belief propagation (BP) schedule. At the transmitter, a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer converts an image into tokens, which are transmitted in multiple low-density parity-check (LDPC) code blocks of fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR). In raster order, a block that BP fails to decode corrupts consecutive token rows, so the interleaver reorders the tokens such that adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks, without additional transmitted bits. At the receiver, after the first BP pass, token recovery fuses the token probabilities given by BP with the predictions of the autoregressive model Emu3-Gen, and the second BP pass decodes each block again with the fused distributions as priors on the information bits. On Kodak24 at 0.5 channel uses per pixel and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 0.15 dB, the second pass removes 92% of the token errors left by token recovery, and interleaving reduces the final token error rate by 88%. At medium to high SNR, the proposed receiver exceeds deep joint source--channel coding baselines with the same channel uses by at least 1.2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio.

title: POST-MIMO: Partition-Oriented Semantic Transmission for MIMO Point Cloud Delivery
authors: Hang Yue; Junlin Chang; Tianqing Zhao; Yulin Zhao; Rongke Liu
abstract: Point clouds have become a fundamental data format for emerging three dimensional (3D) applications, while their wireless delivery remains challenging due to the large data volume and irregular geometric structure. Existing semantic point cloud transmission methods are mainly developed for single-input single-output systems, making them difficult to apply directly to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To address this issue, we propose a partition-oriented semantic transmission framework for MIMO (POST-MIMO) point cloud delivery. POST-MIMO partitions the input point cloud into spatially coherent blocks and aligns them with parallel MIMO streams. Based on this block-aligned representation, the transmitter employs a hierarchical encoder to capture both intra-block local geometry and inter-block global dependency, while the auxiliary side information is transmitted jointly to assist reconstruction. At the receiver, a progressive decoder reconstructs the block geometry in a progressive manner and restores the final point cloud with block-aware adjustment. Experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and lower computational resource consumption than representative reference schemes under the considered MIMO setting.

title: Inter-Frame Predictive Contour Coding for Semantic Map Compression
authors: Runyu Yang; Hyomin Choi; Fabien Racapé; Ivan V. Bajić
abstract: Dynamic semantic maps have become an important intermediate representation for many computer vision applications. Efficient lossless compression of such maps is essential for reducing storage and transmission costs. Existing contour-based semantic map compression methods mainly exploit spatial redundancy within individual frames while largely ignoring the strong temporal correlation between adjacent semantic maps. In this paper, we propose an inter-frame predictive contour coding framework for lossless semantic map compression. The proposed framework first predicts blob positions and label indexes from the reference frame and then performs contour prediction using corresponding chain-code units in the reference contours. A mode selection mechanism is further employed to choose between intra and inter coding according to the estimated coding cost. By exploiting temporal contour redundancy while preserving the advantages of contour-based representation, the proposed framework significantly improves coding efficiency. Experimental results on the VSPW dynamic semantic segmentation dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art lossless semantic map compression methods. Compared with the recent context-adaptive extended chain coding framework, the proposed inter-frame coding achieves an average bitrate reduction of 3.0\% without significant increase in the average encoding time, demonstrating an effective trade-off between compression performance and computational complexity. The source code is made publicly available at https://github.com/InterDigitalInc/LosslessSegmentationMapCompression.

title: Semantic-Assisted Joint Channel Estimation and Symbol Detection for MU-MIMO Systems
authors: Hao Chang; Chentao Yue; Haiyao Yu; Yonghui Li; Branka Vucetic; Wibowo Hardjawana
abstract: This paper presents a semantic-assisted joint channel estimation and symbol detection (Sem-JCED) receiver framework for text transmission in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Sem-JCED integrates a linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) channel estimator, an expectation propagation (EP) symbol detector, and a semantic corrector based on ByT5, a byte-level language model. At each outer iteration, LMMSE estimates the channel from known pilots and data symbol feedback, and EP detects the data symbols. ByT5 then maps the data symbol probabilities to byte probabilities, which provide soft symbol statistics and semantic priors for feedback to LMMSE and EP, respectively, in the next iteration. Simulation results show that Sem-JCED requires about 7~dB lower signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) than conventional JCED to reach a bit error rate (BER) of $1\times10^{-2}$ with four users and four receive antennas, and outperforms maximum-likelihood detection with perfect channel knowledge over the simulated SNR range.

title: Semantic Anchor Communication System for Point Cloud Transmission in Internet of Vehicles
authors: Ruixing Ren; Junhui Zhao; Wei Zhao; Gaoxin Zhang; Xiaoming Wang
abstract: Joint transmission of point cloud geometry and semantics under bandwidth constraints is required for cooperative perception in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Per-point semantics cannot be explicitly preserved by existing geometric compression methods, while interpretable three-dimensional point sets cannot be directly reconstructed via task-feature communication. The paper proposes a spatial semantic anchor communication system. Distinct from global codewords and task features, anchors with explicit coordinates are employed as transmission units. Local shape descriptors and category labels are bound to a unified spatial reference, preserving the correspondence between local position, shape and semantics. At the transmitter, anchor representations are extracted and then converted into digital frames through fixed-point quantization and lossless compression.Atthereceiver,labeledpoint clouds are reconstructed through anchor-constrained local expansion, and pose-aligned multi-view observations are fused. On the 500-frame SemanticPOSS test set, the results demonstrate that spatial semantic anchors enable interpretable joint reconstruction and fusion of geometry and semantics with low transmission overhead.

title: Federated Learning for Semantic Communications over Multiple Access Channels
authors: Yalin E. Sagduyu; Tugba Erpek; Yi Shi
abstract: This paper presents a federated learning (FL) framework for semantic communication (SemCom) over the multiple access channel (MAC), where multiple distributed transmitters simultaneously convey semantic information to a common receiver using end-to-end learned semantic representations. Semantic feature extraction, compression, wireless transmission, and semantic inference are jointly optimized through FL-based SemCom. Unlike conventional SemCom systems that train users independently, simultaneous semantic transmissions over the MAC enable concurrent training of multiple transmitters within the same transmission interval, thereby reducing training overhead and channel usage. Federated semantic aggregation is incorporated with shared and personalized encoder components, allowing transmitters with limited local training data to benefit from semantic representations learned from transmitters possessing larger datasets while preserving local adaptation. Evaluated using the CIFAR-10 dataset over fading channels, the proposed approach maintains high semantic inference accuracy under shared wireless access and significantly improves performance under severe data imbalance. In the meantime, simultaneous semantic transmissions can significantly reduce training overhead while preserving robust semantic performance across distributed transmitters with heterogeneous local datasets. These results highlight the potential of combining FL and SemCom to support scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in future wireless networks.

title: LEMUR: Large scale End-to-end MUltimodal Recommendation
authors: Xintian Han; Honggang Chen; Quan Lin; Jingyue Gao; Xiangyuan Ren; Lifei Zhu; Zhi‐Sheng Ye; Shikang Wu; Xionghang Xie; Xiaochu Gan; Bingzheng Wei; Peng Xu; Zhe Wang; Yu Zheng; J.-L. Lin; Di Wu; Junfeng Ge
venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
abstract: Traditional ID-based recommender systems often struggle with cold-start and generalization challenges. Multimodal recommendation systems, which leverage textual and visual data, offer a promising solution to mitigate these issues. However, existing industrial approaches typically adopt a two-stage training paradigm: first pretraining a multimodal model, then applying its frozen representations to train the recommendation model. This decoupled framework suffers from misalignment between multimodal learning and recommendation objectives, as well as an inability to adapt dynamically to new data. To address these limitations, we propose LEMUR, the first large-scale multimodal recommender system trained end-to-end from raw data. By jointly optimizing both the multimodal and recommendation components, LEMUR ensures tighter alignment with downstream objectives while enabling real-time parameter updates. Constructing multimodal sequential representations from user history often entails prohibitively high computational costs. To alleviate this bottleneck, we propose a novel memory bank mechanism that incrementally accumulates historical multimodal representations throughout the training process. In a 14-day online A/B test on Douyin Search, LEMUR has led to a significant 0.843% reduction in query change rate decay, a 0.558% increase in staytime and a 0.81% improvement in QAUC. Additionally, LEMUR has shown significant gains across key online or offline metrics for Douyin Advertisement, Tiktok Search and Ecom Search. Our results validate the superiority of end-to-end multimodal recommendation in real-world industrial scenarios.

title: Dynamic Feature-Embedding Communication via Codebook Distillation for Federated Recommendation
authors: Mingzhe Han; Jiahao Liu; Dongsheng Li; Jiankui Zhou; Yaqiong Li; Ning Gu; Peng Zhang; Ning Gu; Tun Lu
venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
abstract: Federated recommendation systems commonly protect user privacy by keeping user parameters on local devices, while exchanging item parameters for collaborative model training. However, such item parameters usually model items independently and suffer from both efficiency and effectiveness challenges, making communication costs grow with the item space and limiting cross-item generalization and robustness to noisy feedback. To address these limitations, we propose to model items via shared latent feature embeddings for communication. Residual Quantization (RQ) provides a natural way to instantiate this communication by representing each item with a short sequence of discrete code IDs, i.e., Semantic IDs (SIDs). However, directly applying centralized and static RQ-based recommendation to federated learning is non-trivial due to 1) private and biased historical interactions and 2) evolving collaborative information. We propose RQFedRec, an RQ-based federated recommendation framework for dynamic feature-embedding communication. To construct globally aligned codebooks without accessing private interactions, RQFedRec introduces an information distillation module. Each client first learns item embeddings that encode local collaborative information from private interactions, and then distills such information into feature-indexed codebooks under globally shared SIDs, making sparse and biased local signals more compatible with server aggregation. To adapt to evolving collaborative information, RQFedRec introduces a self-refining SID update module that dynamically refines global SID assignments from aggregated codebooks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RQFedRec improves recommendation performance and reduces communication costs without relying on semantic information, while further benefiting from public semantics when available. Code is available at https://github.com/Mingzhe-Han/RQFedRec.

title: ComPrivDet: Efficient Privacy Object Detection in Compressed Domains Through Inference Reuse
authors: Yunhao Yao; Zhiqiang Wang; Ruiqi Li; Haoran Cheng; Puhan Luo; xiangyang Li
venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) becomes deeply embedded in daily life, users are increasingly concerned about privacy leakage, especially from video, which holds rich, sensitive information. While many techniques can protect privacy, frame-by-frame protection in large-scale video analytics (e.g., smart communities) introduces significant latency. A more efficient solution is to first detect frames containing privacy objects (e.g., faces) and then apply selective protection. However, pixel-domain detection requires fully decoding video frames, incurring decoding overhead. Compressed-domain approaches directly analyze compressed video streams to accelerate inference, but often sacrifice accuracy, and the per-frame processing remains inefficient. Therefore, we propose ComPrivDet, an efficient framework for detecting privacy objects in compressed video by reusing I-frame inference results. ComPrivDet provides a pixel-domain detector on I-frames and a lightweight compressed-domain detector on P/B-frames. Leveraging compressed-domain cues to determine the presence of new objects, ComPrivDet either reuses I-frame results to skip P/B-frame detections or refines them with a lightweight detector. We prototype ComPrivDet on an edge server with an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU. ComPrivDet maintains 99.75% accuracy for private face detection and 96.83% for private license plate detection while skipping over 80% of inferences. It averages 1.36% higher accuracy with 57.23% lower inference latency than pixel-domain baselines, and 10.93% higher accuracy with 44.65% lower latency than compressed-domain baselines.

title: FIERO: Empowering Creative Writing Through Collaborative Game Play
authors: Chu Zhang; XiaoKe Zeng; Jin Zhang; Ruoyu Wen; Vince Siu; Richard William Allen; Ray LC
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
abstract: Creativity often flourishes in collaboration, such as when designers brainstorm a new app together, or storytellers collectively build a world with elements of each person’s narrative. However, collaborative storytelling can have challenges for participants, such as when they disagree about the plot proposed, or when different ideas become fragmented when voiced individually. While current tools for creative collaboration focus on synchronous online text sharing, they often neglect the social dynamics of in-person collaboration critical to creative synergy. To address this, we created FIERO, a multiplayer web-based card game. Physical cards provide tangible scaffolding and social interaction, while the digital interface generates contextual visuals, facilitate group decisions, ensure narrative coherence, and synthesize different idea contributions using Generative AI. Compared against online collaborative writing alone, the game significantly enhanced intuitive stimulation, idea fluency, and novelty generation, and improved the plot coherence of the stories created (N=60). The cards provided creative structure and social engagement, while the application interface provided contextualized augmentation without affecting player agency. This work shows how collaborative play can foster creative support.
